Application.Name: Application
Application.Summary: Events that are related to the lifetime of the application, like starting, pausing, stopped.  A typical app's lifecycle will be: Starting -> Started [-> Pausing -> Paused [-> Resuming -> Resumed]] -> Stopping -> Stopped.

Configuration.Name: Configuration
Configuration.Summary: Reports configuration loading failures, validation attempts, and individual setting results. Successful validation does not imply that a candidate has been applied.

External.Name: External
External.Summary: Reports operations involving external dependencies. Operation outcomes do not automatically determine the application's operating mode.

Dependency.Name: Dependency
Dependency.Summary: Reports failures to locate, load, or construct application components. Resolution outcomes do not automatically determine application mode.

101.Summary: Indicates that application initialization is beginning.
101.Trigger: Emit immediately before beginning application initialization.
Remarks: Framework or bootstrap logging may occur before this event; it does not guarantee that it is the first log record in the process.
Command-line arguments are excluded because they may contain sensitive information.

Arguments.Name: totalMilliseconds
Arguments.Summary: The elapsed time, in milliseconds, from the beginning of application initialization until startup completes.

102.Summary: Indicates that application initialization completed successfully and the application is ready to begin its intended work.
102.Trigger: Emit after all initialization required for the application to begin its intended work has completed successfully.
Remarks: Measure totalMilliseconds from the beginning of initialization represented by Application_Starting to successful completion represented by this event.
The caller supplies the elapsed duration; the logging method does not start or stop a timer.
Successful startup does not guarantee that every optional dependency is healthy.

Arguments.Name: reason
Arguments.Summary: A non-sensitive description of the shutdown cause, or 'Unknown' when the cause is unavailable.

103.Summary: Indicates that application shutdown is beginning.
103.Trigger: Emit when application shutdown begins, before performing shutdown cleanup.
Remarks: The reason describes the known cause of shutdown. Use 'Unknown' when the cause is unavailable rather than inferring one.
This event indicates that shutdown has begun, not that cleanup has completed.

104.Summary: Indicates that application shutdown cleanup has completed.
104.Trigger: Emit after application shutdown cleanup completes, while logging remains available.
Remarks: This event describes completion of application shutdown cleanup; it does not prove that the operating-system process has exited.
Abrupt termination may prevent this event from being emitted.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive logical name of the configuration being validated.

Arguments.Name: validationId
Arguments.Summary: The unique identifier for this validation attempt, shared by its detail and outcome events.

110.Summary: Indicates that validation of a candidate configuration is beginning.
110.Trigger: Emit immediately before evaluating the candidate against its validation rules.
Remarks: Use a new validation identifier for each attempt, including retries and configuration reloads.
A completed evaluation emits exactly one aggregate outcome: Configuration_Validated or Configuration_ValidationFailed.
Per-setting results are optional and can appear between the beginning and aggregate outcome.
Validate a consistent candidate snapshot so all results describe the same configuration.
Cancellation, a validator exception, or process termination can prevent an aggregate outcome. Absence of an outcome does not prove the candidate is invalid.
Calling this method only emits a record; it does not perform validation or enforce event ordering.

111.Message: Setting {SettingName} in configuration {ConfigurationName} passed validation. Validation: {ValidationId}.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The logical configuration name used by the beginning event.

Arguments.Name: validationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of the validation attempt containing this result.

Arguments.Name: settingName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive name or relative path of the validated setting.

111.Summary: Indicates that a setting passed all checks applicable to that setting in this attempt.
111.Trigger: Optionally emit after the setting passes its applicable validation checks.
Remarks: A valid setting does not establish that the entire configuration is valid.
Emit at most one success result for a setting in an attempt, after its applicable checks complete.
A successful check of one rule is insufficient if another applicable rule fails.
This event can describe ordinary validation success and does not necessarily indicate recovery from an earlier failure.
The setting value is intentionally excluded because configuration can contain sensitive information.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The logical configuration name used by the beginning event.

Arguments.Name: validationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of the successfully completed validation attempt.

112.Summary: Indicates that a candidate configuration passed all required validation checks.
112.Trigger: Emit once when the completed evaluation establishes that the candidate satisfies all required validation rules.
Remarks: Use the same configuration name and validation identifier as Configuration_Validating.
Do not emit this event merely because validation finished; a rejected candidate produces Configuration_ValidationFailed.
Success is defined by the declared rules. It does not establish external connectivity unless connectivity was explicitly checked.
This event does not indicate that the candidate has been applied or that application degradation has cleared.
Per-setting success records may be omitted without changing the meaning of this aggregate result.

204.Message: Application has returned to normal operation.
204.Summary: Indicates that the application has recovered from degraded operation.
204.Trigger: Emit when the application leaves degraded mode after all conditions causing reduced functionality have cleared.
Remarks: This event describes recovery of the application instance as a whole. Recovery of one dependency is insufficient if another condition still leaves the application degraded.
Use Application_Started for successful startup; do not emit this event merely because startup completed.
Emit once per transition back to normal operation rather than on every successful health check.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not change application state, deduplicate calls, or verify recovery.
This event does not establish that a load balancer has resumed routing traffic to this instance.
The corresponding degraded-mode event is 401, Application_InDegradedMode.

401.Message: Application is operating in degraded mode. Reason: {Reason}

Arguments.Name: reason
Arguments.Summary: A non-sensitive description of the condition and its effect on application functionality.

401.Summary: Indicates that a recoverable problem has reduced application functionality while allowing operation to continue.
401.Trigger: Emit when the application first establishes degraded operation or transitions from normal to degraded operation.
Remarks: Examples include serving cached data or temporarily disabling an optional feature while a dependency is unavailable.
A failed dependency check alone is insufficient: the application must determine that its functionality is reduced.
Emit once when entering degraded mode rather than repeatedly while the condition persists. The application owns transition detection.
Planned maintenance, deployment draining, and intentional traffic withdrawal do not by themselves constitute degraded operation.
Describe the operational impact without including credentials, connection strings, configuration values, or personal data.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not activate a fallback, change readiness, throttle traffic, or initiate recovery.
Emit 204, Application_InNormalMode, when all conditions causing degraded operation have cleared.

501.Message: Configuration load failed. Configuration: {ConfigurationName}. Source: {SourceName}. Load: {LoadId}. Reason: {ReasonCode}.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive logical name of the configuration being loaded.

Arguments.Name: sourceName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive logical source name. Do not include credentials, connection strings, or sensitive paths or addresses.

Arguments.Name: loadId
Arguments.Summary: The unique identifier of this loading attempt. Use a new identifier for each retry or reload.

Arguments.Name: reasonCode
Arguments.Summary: A stable application-defined failure classification, such as SourceNotFound, SourceAccessDenied, SourceReadFailed, or SourceParseFailed.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception when appropriate for the logging destination, or null when no exception occurred or its details must not be logged.

501.Summary: Reports that an attempt to load configuration failed before a candidate could be obtained for validation.
501.Trigger: Emit when a required configuration-loading attempt fails during source access, reading, parsing, or deserialization.
Remarks: This event describes one failed loading attempt. It does not establish that the application has no working configuration.
A failed reload may leave a previously accepted configuration active. A failed initial load may instead require fallback or shutdown, according to application policy.
A missing optional source is not automatically a loading failure. Emit only when the absence prevents the requested loading attempt from succeeding.

Parsing or deserialization failure prevents obtaining a candidate. A successfully loaded candidate that violates application validation rules belongs to Configuration_ValueIsInvalid and Configuration_ValidationFailed.
Do not emit validation failure solely because loading failed. If no candidate was obtained, validation need not begin.
LoadId identifies a loading attempt. ValidationId identifies a validation attempt. Use a logging scope or trace when correlation across these phases is required.
Use a small documented set of ReasonCode values. Do not include configuration contents, credentials, connection strings, or raw source responses.

Exceptions can reveal source paths, configuration keys, or other sensitive details. Pass the original exception only when appropriate for the logging destination; otherwise pass null. Do not manufacture an exception solely for logging.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
Cancellation and application shutdown are not configuration-loading failures.
Report once at the boundary responsible for the loading attempt. Avoid reporting the same failure again at each calling layer.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not load configuration, retry, reject a candidate, replace active settings, change application mode, or initiate shutdown.

502.Message: External authentication failed. Dependency: {ExternalName}. Operation: {OperationName}. Attempt: {OperationId}. Reason: {ReasonCode}.

Arguments.Name: externalName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical dependency name, without credentials or request-specific data.

Arguments.Name: operationName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the operation whose authentication was rejected.

Arguments.Name: operationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of this individual operation attempt. Use a different identifier for each retry.

Arguments.Name: reasonCode
Arguments.Summary: A stable application-defined classification, such as AuthenticationRejected. Do not include credentials, tokens, or raw response content.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception when appropriate for the configured logging destination, or null when no exception occurred or its details must not be logged.

502.Summary: Reports that an external dependency rejected authentication for an operation attempt.
502.Trigger: Emit when the dependency result establishes an authentication rejection.
Remarks: This event reports the observed rejection. It does not establish that a password is incorrect or identify the underlying credential or policy problem.
An authentication operation that exceeds its deadline belongs to External_OperationTimedOut. An authentication dependency that reports unavailability belongs to External_ServiceUnavailable.
Authorization denial has a separate meaning and belongs to External_AuthorizationFailed.
Use a small documented set of ReasonCode values suitable for grouping. Do not include credentials, tokens, authorization headers, connection strings, or raw authentication responses.

Exceptions may contain sensitive messages or nested details. Pass the original exception only when appropriate for the logging destination; otherwise pass null. Do not manufacture an exception for a normal rejection result.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
Report once at the boundary responsible for the dependency attempt. Avoid reporting the same rejection again at each calling layer.
The event does not change application mode, refresh credentials, retry the operation, or initiate shutdown. Emit application mode events separately when functionality changes.
User cancellation and application shutdown are not authentication rejections.

503.Message: External authorization failed. Dependency: {ExternalName}. Operation: {OperationName}. Attempt: {OperationId}. Reason: {ReasonCode}.

Arguments.Name: externalName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical dependency name, without credentials or request-specific data.

Arguments.Name: operationName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the operation whose permission was denied.

Arguments.Name: operationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of this individual operation attempt. Use a different identifier for each retry.

Arguments.Name: reasonCode
Arguments.Summary: A stable application-defined classification, such as PermissionDenied. Do not include identities, protected resource details, or raw response content.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception when appropriate for the configured logging destination, or null when no exception occurred or its details must not be logged.

503.Summary: Reports that an external dependency denied permission to perform an operation attempt.
503.Trigger: Emit when the dependency result establishes an authorization denial.
Remarks: This event reports the observed permission denial. It does not independently establish that authentication succeeded or identify the policy responsible.
Authentication rejection has a separate meaning and belongs to External_AuthenticationFailed.
Timeouts and dependency unavailability belong to their respective external failure events. Do not classify every unsuccessful result as authorization failure.
Use a small documented set of ReasonCode values suitable for grouping. Do not include tokens, authorization headers, personal identities, protected resource details, or raw response bodies.

Exceptions may contain sensitive messages or nested details. Pass the original exception only when appropriate for the logging destination; otherwise pass null. Do not manufacture an exception for a normal denial result.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
Report once at the boundary responsible for the dependency attempt. Avoid reporting the same denial again at each calling layer.
The event does not grant permission, choose a fallback, change application mode, retry the operation, or initiate shutdown.
Cached fallback must respect the application's authorization and data-access policy. A dependency denial does not itself authorize access to cached data.
User cancellation and application shutdown are not authorization denials.

504.Message: Dependency resolution failed. Dependency: {DependencyName}. Operation: {OperationName}. Resolution: {ResolutionId}. Reason: {ReasonCode}.

Arguments.Name: dependencyName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive logical name of the component being resolved.

Arguments.Name: operationName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive logical operation requiring the component.

Arguments.Name: resolutionId
Arguments.Summary: The unique identifier of this resolution attempt. Use a new identifier for each retry.

Arguments.Name: reasonCode
Arguments.Summary: A stable application-defined classification, such as NotFound, LoadFailed, or ConstructionFailed.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception when appropriate for the logging destination, or null when no exception occurred or its details must not be logged.

504.Summary: Reports that an attempt to locate, load, or construct a requested application component failed.
504.Trigger: Emit when an attempted component resolution cannot supply the requested component.
Remarks: A dependency is an application component, such as a plugin, implementation, or locally loaded provider. This event is not limited to a dependency injection container.
The absence of an optional component is not automatically a failure. Emit when an actual attempt to resolve the requested component fails.
Configuration source loading and parsing failures belong to Configuration_LoadFailed. An operation encountering an unavailable external service belongs to External_ServiceUnavailable.
A successful resolution followed by a failure while using the component is not a resolution failure.
Report once at the boundary responsible for the attempt. Do not report the same failure again at each calling layer.
Use a small documented set of ReasonCode values. Do not include credentials, configuration contents, sensitive paths, or raw exception messages in structured arguments.
Pass the original exception only when appropriate for the logging destination. Do not manufacture an exception solely for logging.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
Cancellation and application shutdown are not dependency resolution failures.
The application may select a fallback, disable a feature, or stop. A resolution failure does not automatically establish degraded application mode.
A later successful resolution does not by itself establish recovery to normal application mode.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not resolve components, retry, select a fallback, change application mode, or initiate shutdown.

506.Message: Setting {SettingName} in configuration {ConfigurationName} failed validation. Reason: {Reason}. Validation: {ValidationId}.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The logical configuration name used by the beginning event.

Arguments.Name: validationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of the validation attempt containing this result.

Arguments.Name: settingName
Arguments.Summary: The non-sensitive name or relative path of the invalid setting.

Arguments.Name: reason
Arguments.Summary: A non-sensitive description of the failed rule and the correction required.

506.Summary: Indicates that a candidate configuration setting failed a validation rule.
506.Trigger: Optionally emit when evaluation establishes that a setting violates an applicable validation rule.
Remarks: Multiple failure details may describe distinct failed rules for the same setting.
The candidate requires correction, but an earlier valid configuration may remain active.
Do not include setting values, credentials, connection strings, or personal data in the reason.
Do not treat an interrupted or unavailable validator as proof that a setting is invalid.
This detail record does not complete the attempt; the aggregate rejection is Configuration_ValidationFailed.
This event does not automatically imply application degradation or require shutdown.

Arguments.Name: configurationName
Arguments.Summary: The logical configuration name used by the beginning event.

Arguments.Name: validationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of the validation attempt that rejected the candidate.

Arguments.Name: reason
Arguments.Summary: A non-sensitive summary of why the candidate failed validation.

507.Summary: Indicates that validation concluded that a candidate configuration is invalid.
507.Trigger: Emit once when an evaluation rejects the candidate because one or more required validation rules failed.
Remarks: Use the same configuration name and validation identifier as Configuration_Validating.
Fail-fast validation may conclude rejection without evaluating every remaining rule.
Group-level or cross-setting rules can fail even when every individually validated setting is valid.
The candidate requires correction. This event does not establish that the application has no usable configuration.
The application decides whether to retain an earlier configuration, disable a feature, or stop.
Cancellation or a validator exception alone does not establish an invalid candidate and must not be reported using this event.
Do not include configuration values or sensitive exception messages in the reason.
Calling this method only emits a record; it does not reject or apply configuration.

601.Message: External operation timed out. Dependency: {ExternalName}. Operation: {OperationName}. Attempt: {OperationId}. Timeout: {TimeoutMilliseconds} milliseconds.

Arguments.Name: externalName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the external dependency, without credentials or request-specific data.

Arguments.Name: operationName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the operation that timed out.

Arguments.Name: operationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of this individual operation attempt. Use a different identifier for each retry.

Arguments.Name: timeoutMilliseconds
Arguments.Summary: The configured timeout budget for this attempt, in milliseconds, rather than its measured elapsed duration.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception associated with the confirmed timeout.

601.Summary: Reports an external operation attempt that failed to complete within its timeout budget.
601.Trigger: Emit when the caller establishes that an external operation attempt timed out.
Remarks: An operation can time out while establishing a connection or while awaiting the result of an already connected operation.
Cancellation alone does not establish a timeout. Do not emit this event for user cancellation or application shutdown.
An OperationCanceledException is appropriate when the caller has established that the operation's timeout caused cancellation.
The exception is required even when Error logging is disabled. Pass the original exception through the logging exception channel rather than converting it to a message-template property.
Emit once per failed attempt at the boundary responsible for reporting the dependency operation. Avoid logging the same timeout again at each layer.
OperationId identifies an individual attempt. A higher-level scope or trace can correlate several attempts belonging to the same logical operation.
TimeoutMilliseconds describes the configured budget, not measured elapsed time. Cancellation observation and cleanup can occur after that budget expires.
A timeout establishes that the caller did not obtain a result within its budget. It does not establish that the remote operation stopped or that it produced no side effects.
This event reports a failed operation attempt. It does not establish that the dependency is permanently unavailable or that administrator intervention is immediately required.
Emit Application_InDegradedMode separately only when application functionality becomes reduced. Emit Application_InNormalMode only when the application subsequently recovers from that degradation.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not cancel operations, retry requests, manage a circuit breaker, or change application state.

602.Message: External service unavailable. Dependency: {ExternalName}. Operation: {OperationName}. Attempt: {OperationId}. Reason: {ReasonCode}.

Arguments.Name: externalName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the dependency, without credentials or request-specific data.

Arguments.Name: operationName
Arguments.Summary: The stable logical name of the operation the dependency could not serve.

Arguments.Name: operationId
Arguments.Summary: The identifier of this individual operation attempt. Use a different identifier for each retry.

Arguments.Name: reasonCode
Arguments.Summary: A stable application-defined classification of the observed availability failure, such as ServiceUnavailable. Do not include response bodies or exception messages.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The original exception associated with the availability failure, or null when the dependency returned an unavailable result without throwing.

602.Summary: Reports that an external dependency could not serve an operation because of an observed availability failure.
602.Trigger: Emit when the caller receives an explicit unavailable result or establishes that a dependency exception represents an availability failure.
Remarks: This event describes availability from the caller's perspective for one operation attempt. It does not establish that the service is unavailable to every caller.
Use OperationTimedOut for an operation that exceeded its timeout budget. Do not emit both events merely to describe the same timeout.
Do not classify every unsuccessful response or exception as service unavailability. Authentication, authorization, invalid requests, and business rejections have different meanings.
A locally open circuit breaker does not establish the dependency's current availability because the operation was not attempted.
ReasonCode is an application-defined classification suitable for grouping and alerting. Use a small documented set of values rather than request-specific text.
Pass the original exception when one exists. Pass null for an unavailable result returned without an exception; do not manufacture an exception solely for logging.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
Emit once per failed attempt at the boundary responsible for reporting the dependency operation. Use a higher-level scope or trace to correlate retries.
A failed attempt does not automatically change application mode. Emit Application_InDegradedMode separately when functionality becomes reduced and Application_InNormalMode after recovery.
User cancellation and application shutdown are not availability failures.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not retry requests, operate a circuit breaker, or change application state.

Arguments.Name: exception
Arguments.Summary: The exception that reached the application boundary and prevents normal operation from continuing.

701.Summary: Reports an unrecoverable exception at an application boundary.
701.Trigger: Emit when an exception reaches a top-level application boundary and the application cannot continue normally.
Remarks: This event is intended for application-ending failures, not recoverable operation or request failures.
Unhandled means that lower-level application code did not recover from the exception; a top-level boundary may catch it to report the failure and initiate shutdown.
Pass the original exception so logging providers retain access to its type, stack trace, and inner exceptions.
The exception travels through the logging exception channel and is not a message-template property.
The exception argument must not be null, even when Critical logging is disabled.
Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record. It does not terminate the process, initiate shutdown, or install exception handlers.
Abrupt termination may prevent this event from being emitted or flushed.

LowLevel.Name: LowLevel
LowLevel.Summary: Positive, low-level lifecycle related app events like Start, Pause, Stop, reading Configuration/Settings, Dependency initialization - Application plumbing, no intervention required by anyone

OperationalInformation.Name: OperationalInformation
OperationalInformation.Summary: Positive, normal run, expected, operational events like calling an external service, running diagnostics -  No intervention required by anyone

OperationalWarning.Name: OperationalWarning
OperationalWarning.Summary: Normal, run, expected, operational warning like when an app is switching to InMaintenance, when a diagnostic test failed validation, or there's a mismatch of version.  - No immediate intervention required by anyone, but should be investigated anyhow.

RecoverableWarning.Name: RecoverableWarning
RecoverableWarning.Summary: Internal, recoverable problems, where the app can continue to work but with limited functionality, like the app is running in DegradedMode, the app has the ability to recover from the incident.  Admin intervention is not a necessity but is a good idea to monitor the situation.

UnrecoverableWarning.Name: UnrecoverableWarning
UnrecoverableWarning.Summary: Internal, unrecoverable problems, like un-usable configuration, failed authentication/authorization to a service, the app can continue to work but with limited functionality, and an intervention by an admin is required.

Exceptional.Name: Exceptional
Exceptional.Summary: Failures involving external dependencies, such as operation timeouts or unavailable services. Application impact and the need for intervention depend on recovery options, persistence, and operational context.
